title: Race Conditions & Mailbox Hygiene: Why demonitor(Ref, [flush]) is Mandatory
solutionExplanation: Demonstrates the monitor race condition and why demonitor(Ref, [flush]) is mandatory to prevent Save Queue memory pollution.

otpDocCards.description: Disables monitor and purges any already-delivered DOWN message for MonitorRef from mailbox.
otpDocCards.complexityNote: O(M) scan of mailbox messages, but O(1) in typical clean mailboxes.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is `erlang:demonitor(MRef, [flush])` mandatory over plain `erlang:demonitor(MRef)` when finishing a synchronous call?

options.label: If the worker terminated right as it sent its reply, its 'DOWN' message is already queued in the mailbox; [flush] purges it atomically to prevent mailbox memory leaks.
options.explanation: Correct! Plain demonitor only prevents future DOWN messages. If the DOWN message arrived before demonitor was called, [flush] scans and deletes it, keeping the mailbox pristine.

options.label: Plain demonitor crashes the target worker process.
options.explanation: demonitor does not affect the target worker; it only affects the caller.

options.label: [flush] is required to save the return value to ETS.
options.explanation: demonitor has nothing to do with ETS tables.
